context:
Establish one stable interpreter for the shared hook so no worktree can capture it.

Options, cheapest first:
- Have make worktree-create and worktree-remove leave the hook alone, and install it once from the primary clone against the primary venv. Document that `pre-commit install` must never be run from a worktree.
- Or point the hook at an interpreter that outlives any single worktree, so removal cannot dangle it.
- Or add a repair step to make worktree-remove that reinstalls the hook from the primary clone after removing a worktree.

Whichever is chosen, add a check to make agent-write-preflight (scripts/agent_write_preflight.sh) that fails loudly when the hook's INSTALL_PYTHON does not exist. Silent degradation to "no hooks ran" is the real hazard; a dangling hook should be noisy, not a fallback.

Do not solve this by removing the hook or by teaching agents to pass --no-verify.
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 in the primary clone at /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.

.git/hooks/pre-commit is generated by `pre-commit install` and hardcodes an absolute interpreter:

    INSTALL_PYTHON=/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.wt-worktree-audit/.venv/bin/python

That worktree was removed when #1937 merged. The path no longer exists.

Git hooks live in the COMMON git dir, so a single .git/hooks/pre-commit is shared by the primary clone and every linked worktree. Running `pre-commit install` from inside any worktree rewrites the shared hook to point at THAT worktree's venv. Removing the worktree leaves the hook dangling for everyone.

Observed failure mode, in this session: every `git commit` printed

    `pre-commit` not found.  Did you forget to activate your virtualenv?

and aborted. The generated hook falls back to `command -v pre-commit`, so the outcome depends entirely on whether a venv happens to be on PATH. Commits either abort with a misleading message or silently run no hooks at all. Both are bad: this repo gates real things there (corpus-inventory drift check, agent write preflight, git identity audit, ruff, codespell).

Workaround used during the corpus trust cut: prefix each commit with an explicit PATH export pointing at a live venv. Not discoverable, and easy to forget -- forgetting means committing with no hooks.
